facts.raw_span: A 65-year-old man with benign prostatic hyperplasia
prostate-specific antigen level was 0.796 ng/mL
Uroflowmetry revealed reduced urine flow, prolonged micturition time, and obstructive findings
He was started on oral Alfuzosin 10 mg once daily
loss of appetite and malaise, followed by generalized pruritus, dark urine, and jaundice
He denied use of aspirin, acetaminophen, or herbal medicines
no history of liver disease
leukocyte count 5.8 K/μL
total bilirubin 7.6 mg/dL (0.2–1.2)
Abdominal ultrasonography showed normal liver, gallbladder, common bile duct, and intrahepatic bile ducts

concepts.why: The patient developed jaundice and elevated liver enzymes after starting Alfuzosin, suggesting a drug-induced liver injury.
The patient has a history of benign prostatic hyperplasia, which is supported by the prostate-specific antigen level and uroflowmetry results.
The patient has reduced urine flow and obstructive findings on uroflowmetry, suggesting a urinary obstruction.
The patient has elevated bilirubin levels and pruritus, suggesting cholestasis.
The patient has elevated liver enzymes, suggesting hepatocellular injury.
The patient developed liver injury after starting Alfuzosin, suggesting Alfuzosin-induced hepatotoxicity.
The patient has elevated bilirubin levels and pruritus, but no clear cause, suggesting idiopathic cholestasis.
The patient has reduced urine flow and obstructive findings on uroflowmetry, suggesting urinary retention.
It explains the normal liver, gallbladder, common bile duct, and intrahepatic bile ducts findings on abdominal ultrasonography in the context of cholestasis.

rationales.F03: Uroflowmetry findings are consistent with urinary obstruction.

rationales.F05: The patient's symptoms are consistent with liver injury and cholestasis.
rationales.F06: The absence of other medications or herbal supplements reduces the likelihood of other causes of liver injury.
rationales.F07: The absence of a history of liver disease reduces the likelihood of pre-existing liver conditions.
rationales.F09: Elevated AST levels are consistent with liver injury.
rationales.F10: Elevated ALT levels are consistent with liver injury.
rationales.F11: Elevated bilirubin levels are consistent with liver injury and cholestasis.
rationales.F12: Normal abdominal ultrasonography reduces the likelihood of obstructive causes of jaundice.
